question: Are my minimum-stay restrictions turning away demand in July?
lenses_active: L3b MinLOS vs demand LOS · L2 Unsold risk · L4 OTA parity
summary: Trade-off, not a mistake: July's MinLOS 4 captures 7-night searchers but turns away ~38,000 short-stay searches. Direct is clearly cheaper than the OTAs (−27%), so the channel is healthy: the real question is whether long-stay demand is enough to fill July, especially the already-soft last week.

charts.caption: Left: searches in the area (20 km) per week — peak mid-June (~16,300), minimum in the last week of July (4,300). Right: length of stay — 7 nights is #1 (26,114), but 1–3 nights combined weigh in at 38,441. Average lead time 28 → 92 days. Destination data.

lenses.title: L3b — MinLOS vs demand LOS
lenses.rule: Rule: short-stay search share (1–3 nights) ≥ 40% AND MinLOS on those dates > 3 nights → matchable demand turned away.
lenses.callout: Reading: in July you enforce MinLOS 4 on every date. You capture 7-night searchers well (the area's #1 search), but anyone searching for 1–3 nights — 53% of searches — can't even see you. It's a legitimate seasonal choice; it only becomes a problem if long-stay demand doesn't fill you up. It's not a mistake: it's a trade-off to decide on.

lenses.title: L2 — Unsold risk (crossed with the restriction)
lenses.rule: Rule: low demand + inside the booking window. Here compounded by MinLOS 4.
lenses.note: The last week of July has the lowest demand of the period (4,300 searches, −74% vs the peak) but keeps MinLOS 4. It's the riskiest combination: low demand and a high filter on short stays exactly when flexibility would help. Option: relax MinLOS on the last third of July if pickup stays weak.

lenses.title: L4 — OTA parity (test stay Jul 17–21)
lenses.note: Direct is the cheapest channel, by a wide margin. An advantage worth pushing hard on the site. No parity issue.

date_map.heading: Restriction map — minimum stay
date_map.note: No sold-out dates in the period: the constraint here isn't availability but minimum length of stay. July is entirely MinLOS 4.

limits: An area-demand vs availability/rules/price diagnostic, not a revenue management system. With SimpleBooking data alone it does not see actual on-the-books figures or pickup, real competitor rates (only OTA parity), or an events source. The short-stay share is area demand: some of it searches other hotels anyway. The pointers are conditional options, not prescriptions — long-stay may be a deliberate seasonal strategy.
events: Area demand rises sharply in mid-June and the first weeks of July: can you confirm whether there are events or fairs in the area that justify the higher MinLOS (e.g. the jump to MinLOS 4 on June 26–27)? The skill detects the curve but not the cause.
options: Consciously decide the MinLOS 4 trade-off: keep it to protect long-stay, or relax it to capture short stays.
Consider lowering MinLOS on the last third of July (weaker demand) if pickup doesn't pick up.
Push the direct-vs-OTA advantage (−27%) from the parity check on the site.
Turn on a scheduled scan to monitor how the long-stay weeks are filling up.
